title: Upper Trapezius Kneading
summary: The soft tissue of the upper trapezius is gently lifted and rhythmically kneaded between the fingers and palm.
goal: Work the bulk of the upper trapezius without pressing on the cervical vertebrae or bony shoulder structures.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of kneading the upper trapezius.
startingPosition: The shoulder is relaxed. The practitioner's hand rests on the muscular ridge between the base of the neck and shoulder.
instructions: Locate the soft muscular area between the neck and shoulder.
Gently grasp the tissue between the fingers and heel of the hand.
Lift slightly and compress the muscle comfortably.
Release the pressure without losing contact.
Progress in small sections along the muscle.
direction: Work progressively along the muscular ridge from the base of the neck toward the shoulder.
tips: Grasp muscle tissue rather than pinching the skin.
mistakes: Moving onto the side of the neck.
warning: Avoid deep kneading with acute pain, recent injury, or neurological symptoms. Stop if pressure produces radiating pain.
telegramCaption: Controlled kneading of the soft upper trapezius.
